verdict.rationale: Angular's first-party docs describe built-in Signals for reactive state updates and built-in dependency injection, which are native primitives for managing state without a third-party library. However, the evidence never explicitly says these handle app-wide shared or global state. missing for 10: explicit documentation of global/shared application state patterns (e.g. signal-based services via DI), depth on store-like capabilities, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage global application state using built-in primitives without adding a third-party library

citations.quote: Reactive and fast state updates with fine-grained reactivity based on Angular Signals
organized yet modular thanks to Angular components and dependency injection
